### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **11** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/sdui-parser`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **63** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **21** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-ai-agent-authoring.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/types.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **21** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/validate-ai-agent-authoring.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/types.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `943a21534c96684329ff11ef475c9987036a0073` — the merge of head `49ef13a518dd486eeef521971583f109f098f590` into base `51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 943a21534c96684329ff11ef475c9987036a0073 && git checkout 943a21534c96684329ff11ef475c9987036a0073
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501 49ef13a518dd486eeef521971583f109f098f590 && git checkout -B drift-repro 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501 && git merge --no-ff 49ef13a518dd486eeef521971583f109f098f590

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 51b43a8dc45fef9d86229509ab6b2679ffa9d501` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `49ef13a518dd486eeef521971583f109f098f590`
Local-runs: none

PR #22874 (card #22340, stage S2: `allowOrgOverride` becomes `allowEnvironmentOverlay`, with the objectui pin). The landing record for this head, read at 2026-10-12T05:20Z. Inputs and nothing else: the card body and its 21 comments (ruling `6073921182`, the pre-build review `6109457426`, the re-measure `6109312314` and its acceptance `6109343061`, the claim `6109485204`, the dev reports `6112207139` and `6118005809`, the seat's `6112246741`, `6117020961` and `6118028021`, the `domain:ui` pointer `6116505303`); ADR-0131 D6, ADR-0087 D2/D3 and its level ruling, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/check-future-spec-major.mjs` and `.changeset/pre.json` on `origin/main` (`51b43a8dc4`); the PR body and the net diff against the merge base `018b077fbf` (162 files, +1509 / -649); objectui at `e5311165a8d6` by `git grep` in a scratch clone; the head's check-runs through REST. Every reading below was re-taken from the trees and the diff; the seat's and the dev's conclusions were read for what they assert and not adopted. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The declaration and the tombstone — holds.**
- `MetadataTypeRegistryEntryBaseSchema.allowEnvironmentOverlay: z.boolean().default(false)` carries the describe the pre-build review fixed, word for word ("Whether an environment may overlay an item of this type that a managed package ships (ADR-0131 D6 regime O). Decides the save door, the managed-content seal on write and on read, and Studio's write gate; the OS_METADATA_WRITABLE hatch does not reach a managed item. Default false."), and a TSDoc that names regime O, the four doors, the hatch's limit, the default and ADR-0005's one-whitelist rule. ADR-0131 D6 on `origin/main` names regime O as "an environment row of the same name replaces the managed item whole" over exactly the five presentational types, so the describe says what the ADR decided.
- `allowOrgOverride` is `retiredKey(...)` on the same base schema (the file imports `retiredKey` and already tombstones three `MetadataPluginConfig` keys the same way). Its prescription reads "was renamed to `allowEnvironmentOverlay` (ADR-0131 D6) … Rename the key to `allowEnvironmentOverlay`; the value is unchanged." It carries no version word, so it contradicts nothing in the changeset. Read against ADR-0087's level ruling ("a tombstone names the npm release it ships in, never the protocol major"): the tree publishes `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 and `check-future-spec-major` refuses any `@objectstack/spec` citation above that major, while the release this ships in is `18.0.0-next.*` under pre mode, so no version spelling satisfies both the ruling and the gate; the version-free prescription that names the deciding ADR is the honest form, and the TSDoc's "in 18" is the protocol major (`toMajor: 18`), a number the gate deliberately does not match. Judged correct.
- All 28 `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` rows spell the new key (counted in the diff: object, field, hook, seed, picklist, mapping, view, page, dashboard, app, action, report, dataset, flow, job, datasource, external_catalog, api, translation, email_template, doc, book, permission, position, capability, agent, tool, skill); the true set is exactly view, dashboard, report, translation, email_template; no value moved. The generated baselines agree: `authorable-surface/kernel.json` gains the new row and marks the old one `[RETIRED]`; `authorable-defaults/kernel.json` reads `allowEnvironmentOverlay = false`; `authorable-surface.base.json` is untouched.
- `supportsOverlay` keeps its name; its TSDoc, its registry describe, the `GetMetaTypesResponse` describe, the `MetadataTypeInfoResponse` describe and the `contracts/metadata-service.ts` TSDoc all say the one thing it gates — the removal carve-out, "removes no managed definition, and changes what is served for `permission` alone; it opens no save and it decides no read" — in the wording #22833 landed on `main` (`protocol.ts:16155` there). The `customizationPolicies` prescription, `kernel/index.ts`, `email-template.zod.ts` and the unreleased D3 `18.metadata-customization-protocol-retired` now name the environment overlay and the new key; none still presents the per-organization axis as live.

**2. The wire, both arms — holds; the read-side trap is closed.**
- `getMetaTypes`, registry arm: `allowEnvironmentOverlay: base.allowEnvironmentOverlay || isEnvOverridden` and `overrideSource` derived from `base.allowEnvironmentOverlay`; the `...base` spread carries the same key at the registry value and the elevated value overwrites it. Synthesised arm (a runtime type with no registry row): `allowEnvironmentOverlay: writableOverrides.has(singular)`. The old name is written on neither arm. `api/protocol.zod.ts` renames the field with the honest describe of the elevated value ("True when the registry grants … or when OS_METADATA_WRITABLE names the type (overrideSource env), which opens the type's writes of items no managed package ships and never a managed item (ADR-0131 D6)") and `overrideSource`'s describe names the new field; `api/metadata.zod.ts` corrects `supportsOverlay`. The wire pin (`protocol-meta-types-rich.test.ts`) asserts both arms under the hatch (`hook` on the spread arm, `theme` on the synthesised arm), `overrideSource` on each, and `not.toHaveProperty('allowOrgOverride')` on every entry, with a presence control for each arm; S1's five-type file asserts the new key and the old name's absence on both topologies.
- Readers, re-taken on the head tree: `git grep allowOrgOverride` over `packages/**/src/**` and `examples/**`, tests and migration entries excluded, finds nine lines — the tombstone, its prescription and TSDoc, the registry's naming note, the rationale fragment, and four history comments (`protocol.ts:16057`, `sys-metadata-repository.ts:1768` and `:2034`, `rest-server.ts:7029`). No code reference remains, in `.ts` or `.tsx`. The three set readers read the new key: `protocol.ts` `OVERLAY_ALLOWED_TYPES` (`if (!entry.allowEnvironmentOverlay) continue`), `getMetaTypes` on both arms, and `sys-metadata-repository.ts` `OVERLAY_ALLOWED_TYPES` (its registry filter now reads `e.allowEnvironmentOverlay`); `isOverlayAllowed`, `registryAllowsOverlay`, `isSealedManagedItem`, `declinesStoredRow` and `assertAllowed` derive from those sets and did not need to move. The absence pin (`metadata-type-registry-allow-org-override-absence.test.ts`, `repo` project, listed in `vitest.repo-tests.json`) walks `packages/**/*.ts` and `examples/*/src/**/*.ts` by AST, counts identifiers and quoted keys and never comments or strings, exempts the tombstone by shape alone, counts the refusal pin apart as a required positive control, and asserts the three hand-renamed files are found under the new name — so a reader left on the old name goes red rather than reading `undefined`. The one live sentence outside those files, `packaged-base-regime.ts:407`, names the new key, as do the repository's two refusal sentences and `codeOnlyCreateError` / `codeOnlyOverrideError`; no code or status changed.

**3. The kit — holds; `check-adr-0087-registration` holds on the diff.**
- `entries/retired-keys/18.kernel__MetadataTypeRegistryEntry__allowOrgOverride.ts` exports exactly `kernel/MetadataTypeRegistryEntry:allowOrgOverride`, the string the authorable-surface gate reads, with the Q1 A rationale (tombstone + entry + D3, no D2, no seam that ever runs).
- One D3 entry, `18.metadata-type-registry-allow-org-override-renamed.ts`, covering the registry key and the `GET /api/v1/meta/types` field together, with a backtick-free `surface`, the five-type truth in `replacement`, the read-side warning in `reason` and a behaviour-unchanged `acceptanceCriteria`; its `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment sits in `registry.ts.template` at order 94, between `metadata-plugin-additional-types-retired` and `object-grid-default-filters-retired`.
- No D2 conversion, as ruling Q1 A requires; no `registry.ts`, `spec-changes.json` or upgrade guide is committed (generated, git-ignored).
- `18.metadata-customization-protocol-retired.ts` now names "ADR-0005's environment overlay (opt-in via `allowEnvironmentOverlay` …, stored as environment-wide `sys_metadata` rows …)", and its fragment in the template says "environment overlay".
- The gate's rule, read from its header: a changeset the PR adds that declares breaking must carry one marker; `registered` requires every id to resolve at HEAD and at least one to be new in the diff. The rename changeset's marker reads `registered metadata-type-registry-allow-org-override-renamed`, an id this diff creates; the retired-keys string is not an id the gate resolves and is named in the changeset body instead. The console changeset's marker reads `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` and its body carries no FROM / TO rewrite of its own (the rename's prescription lives in the rename changeset, which the marker text says). Both `Check Changeset` runs on the head are green.

**4. The changeset — every sentence true to the diff.** `.changeset/22340-registry-allow-environment-overlay.md`: `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` at `major`; the BREAKING banner; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, one of the two readings `clause2-line.mjs` accepts for a diff that both widens (a new published key) and narrows (a retired one); the FROM / TO table for a registry entry, a reader of one and each `entries[]` item of `GET /api/v1/meta/types`; the one-line fix; the five-type truth; the hatch sentence; the read-side warning; the `supportsOverlay` correction; the who-is-affected reading; the kit. Each claim was checked against the diff: the 28 rows, both writer arms, the three refusal sentences quoted (`packaged-base-regime.ts:407`, `sys-metadata-repository.ts:1900`, `protocol.ts` code-only errors), the `overrideSource` describe, the D3 id and the retired-keys string. Level: see ②.

**5. The pin — holds.**
- `.objectui-sha` reads `e5311165a8d6aa77b5cb7d9fd05da8451a2c21aa`, the merge of objectui#12168 (carrying objectui#12141), fetched into a scratch ref and read there.
- objectui at that commit: `allowOrgOverride` occurs in 5 files, every one history — three `CHANGELOG.md` and two changesets (`11808-readonly-package-card.md`, `12141-allow-environment-overlay.md`, whose FROM / TO names the rename and states "no alias window and no dual read"); zero source or test hits. `allowEnvironmentOverlay` is read in 12 non-test source files under `packages/app-shell/src/views/` (`DirectoryPage.tsx:171/175/458`, `EmbeddedItemEditor.tsx:104`, `PageShell.tsx:100`, `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:394/395/422`, `ResourceEditPage.tsx:1442/1443/1882/1884/1885`, `ResourceListPage.tsx:428`, `registry.ts:462/464/472`, `useMetadata.ts:84`, `i18n.ts`, `previews/PicklistPreview.tsx`, `BuilderLanding.tsx`), 187 hits in 75 files overall; control `allowRuntimeCreate` reads on the same files. So the pinned console reads exactly the field this PR's `getMetaTypes` writes, and landing the two together keeps the five overlay types writable in Studio; the ruled-out dual read is absent.
- The bump follows PR #22794's shape: `console-e5311165a8d6.md` (`@objectstack/console` minor, derived from objectui's 21 releasing changesets, the four declared-breaking objectui changes each answered in the marker, the one undeclared commit listed by subject), `objectui-pin-citations-e5311165a8d6.md` (`@objectstack/spec` patch, `Clause-②: no`), `sdui.manifest.json` (one input description changed, the record activity feed's `showCompleted`), `scripts/sdui-manifest.record.json` (sha, modules root, date, hash), `packages/sdui-parser/objectui-lockstep.json` (rev, revDate, recordedAgainstPin only), `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx` (the `span` describe's pin). Every changed line in the spec-source pin hunks (`component.zod.ts`, `view.zod.ts`, `action.zod.ts`, `dataset.zod.ts`, `functional-completeness.ts`, the six `*-unit-in-key.ts` entries, the three test files) is a comment, a string literal or the `span` describe's pin sha; no key, default, enum member or export moves.

**6. The merge of `main` — both sides kept.** `main`'s side between the two merges (`12b9daf749..018b077fbf`) touched `email-template.zod.ts` (+6), `liveness/README.md` (+1) and the regenerated `email-template.mdx`. Line-checked on the head: every line `main` added to `liveness/README.md` is present verbatim; of the six `main` added to `email-template.zod.ts`, five are verbatim and the sixth ("… a Studio save overrides a built-in default at environment level. No") is present reflowed over two lines with the branch's parenthetical ("(`allowEnvironmentOverlay: true` in the metadata registry). No") inserted — #15205's registry-read sentence and S2's key reference both stand. The net diff against `018b077fbf` on those two files shows only the rename and that parenthetical, so no hunk of `main`'s side is lost. `main` has moved nine commits since (to `51b43a8dc4`); the dev reports a clean `merge-tree`, not re-measured here, and the queue rebuilds the merge in any case.

**7. CI — every check on the head is green or an expected skip.** Read through REST at this act: 42 check-runs, 42 completed, 39 `success`, 3 `skipped`, none failed, none still running. The seven required contexts are all `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (with its `source gates`, `consumer gates`, `debt ledger` and `workspace` legs), `Test Core` (all six shards and the aggregate — so the suite-duration ceiling and the `connector-author-shape.test.ts` timeout of #22929 did not land on this head), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (three shards and the aggregate), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Also green: `Console Pin Gate` (objectui built at `e5311165a8` against this tree), `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Spec property liveness`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, both `Check Changeset` runs, and both runs of each PR-context guard (the closing-card claim, the single-writer path, the part-of keyword and the no-second-PR guard). The three skips are expected: `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, and the `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` jobs of the second `pr-automation` run (the body edit), whose first runs on this same head are `success`. The Vercel status is "Canceled by Ignored Build Step", reported as success.

### ② Semver level

`major` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, and that is the level the pre-mode rules give. `.changeset/pre.json` on `origin/main` reads `mode: pre, tag: next`. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s header (the authority ADR-0087's level ruling defers to) states the RC exemption: in pre mode a `major` only ever produces an `X.0.0-tag.N` pre-release and "accumulating the next major's breaking changes is precisely what an RC window is for", so the launch-window guard stands aside. The precedent the PR cites, `.changeset/22572-flow-binding-name-dollar-refused.md`, declares `@objectstack/spec: major` with the same sentence, and `origin/main` carries 21 changesets declaring a major. ADR-0087's "pre-GA ships `minor`" is the launch-window rule the exemption suspends while the window is in pre mode; the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition, which that ruling makes the mandatory carriers, are both present. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is consistent with `major` (a `yes` takes at least `minor`; a narrowing is breaking), and the declaration appears once on the PR body and once in the rename changeset. The console changeset's `minor` and the citations changeset's `patch` are the right levels for a pin move and a comment-only re-measure.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **One prose slip in the writer, not in the contract.** The new comment above `getMetaTypes`'s registry arm (`protocol.ts`, the "ONE wire spelling, on BOTH arms" paragraph) ends "so no entry carries `allowEnvironmentOverlay`, the spelling retired in 18" — it names the new key where it means `allowOrgOverride`. The code two lines below writes `allowEnvironmentOverlay` on every entry, the wire pin asserts it, and the absence pin ignores comments, so nothing reads the sentence; it is a one-word fix for the next change that touches the file (S3 is the nearest), not a reason to move this head. Recorded so it is not re-found.
- **Independence.** `Reviewed-by` names the seat session that also holds the claim; the verdict was rendered by an isolated reviewing subagent of that session with the inputs listed above and no others, and every finding here was re-derived from the trees and the diff rather than adopted from the seat's `6118028021` or the dev's reports. The dev identity on `Implemented-by` is the branch, as a `mode:subagent` dispatch records it.
- **Not judged here, by the brief's inputs:** cloud's two test helpers (`service-ai-studio` `write-door.ts` and `metadata-tools.test.ts`) stay NOT MEASURED and recorded on the card (`6109343061` item 5) for a seat that reaches cloud; the governed text (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 7, `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, ADR-0005) still names the old key on this head and is S3's, as planned — no governed-surface path is in this PR's file list, and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green.
- **Size and state:** 162 files, 2158 changed lines (generated included), under the 3,000 line; head repo is the base repo; the PR is draft with auto-merge unarmed, as the order requires until this record.
- **`check:platform-checklist`** is reported red on `main` and on this head on eight findings in `areas/access-security.json`, `areas/attachments-storage.json` and `areas/search.json`; none of those files is in this PR's diff, and the reported absent symbols (`anonymousFormIntakeOrgScopeRefusal`, `envWideRawViewRows`, `canEdit`, `countable`) are not touched by it. Not this diff's.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-22340-s2-rename`
Reviewed-by: `session_01KNKBCRDJCu5tGy3TEbvtrF`

**VERDICT: PASS**

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [38207850018](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/38207850018) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (6/6)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/38207850018/job/114675288856)** — 失败步骤: Check this shard's timing drift（日志不可读，点进 job 看）
